title: Planning versus fate
summary: Wilson and Hinton weigh Hawkins's view that good things come unplanned against the need to work toward objectives.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: That's amazing. Well, look, I'd like to wind this up with you in the next 10 or 15 minutes.

Like Coleman says, we've wasted time talking about this thing, you might as well just go ahead and do it, and if it happens, it happens, and if if it doesn't happen, it doesn't. But I still think you have to do what you can to the best of your understanding to work toward objectives.
Well, one has to always do the best one can.

Sure, you've got to have objectives, you can't just work aimlessly; because what he's saying, you waste time when you're setting objectives and even if you get it, it's no good, and the good stuff is the stuff you don't work toward, it just comes out of the blue sky.
But I think you need both.
Yeah, you do need both. You need to
work, it's good to work towards objectives. If you get it or you don't, it's still good.
You still get lucky accidents, too, Get 'em both. sometimes. So that takes care of that.
